📡 Russia’s Medvedev slams US double standards on Iran’s nuclear program

📌 Moscow, IRNA – Deputy chairman of the Russian Security Council strongly criticized the US for its contradictory and hypocritical approach to Iran’s nuclear program.

In an article titled “State Sovereignty and Nuclear Weapons: International Legal Aspects of Ensuring National Security” for the Moscow Journal of International Law, Dmitry Medvedev argued that appeals to the nuclear non-proliferation regime are frequently invoked for political purposes, disregarding the reality on the ground.
​
Medvedev pointed out that Washington attacked Iran under the pretext of defending the non-proliferation regime, despite Tehran’s clear commitment to its obligations.
​
“Through its complete openness to negotiations and inspections in the field of peaceful nuclear energy, Tehran has demonstrated, not in words but in deeds, that it has no desire to possess nuclear weapons. And even in the face of direct threats of nuclear bombardment and aggression, including against civilian nuclear facilities, the Iranians have not yet renounced their status as a non-nuclear state under the NPT,” he stated.
​
The Russian official emphasized that Washington’s actions “demonstrate the double standards of American non-proliferation policy and are driven exclusively by geopolitical considerations: restrictions are imposed on unfriendly states.”
​
Elsewhere in the article, the Russian official pointed to the NPT and stated that the text of the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation is self-sufficient. However, the document’s status undermines its enforcement, which depends on the degree of loyalty of one of the great powers: “The universality of the NPT is gradually being eroded, not by any flaws in the treaty's text, but by the uneven nature of its political application.”
​
“When the scope of permissible nuclear activities effectively depends on whether a state is an adversary or an ally of a major power or a military bloc, the non-proliferation regime loses some of its normative persuasiveness. Formally, the law remains uniform, but political practice makes its application selective.”
​
Withdrawal from the NPT automatically frees countries of their non-proliferation obligations: “A state’s withdrawal from the NPT removes its responsibility under international law for developing nuclear weapons,” Medvedev added.

Yesterday, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpoge, together with Claude, presented a formal proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. It is one of the most famous mathematical problems in history, one that mathematicians have been unable to solve for 167 years.

In short, the Riemann Hypothesis describes a fundamental pattern in the distribution of prime numbers. It is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems, and the Clay Mathematics Institute offers $1 million for its solution.

The proof has not yet been officially accepted. However, the published materials have already undergone several serious independent technical reviews. If the mathematical community confirms the result, it would be a historic event.

But what matters more here is not the mathematics itself.

If AI really helped solve a problem in just a few weeks that generations of the world's best mathematicians had unsuccessfully worked on for more than a century and a half, it means we're approaching a point where artificial intelligence is beginning to do more than just use existing knowledge — it's starting to create new knowledge.

Now imagine that the next step happens within AI itself.

Today, solving some complex problem might require, say, 10,000 GPUs. Tomorrow, AI discovers a new algorithm that allows it to solve the same problem using 100 GPUs. Then 10. Then just one.

This is still a hypothetical scenario. But if AI really starts independently finding ways to radically improve the efficiency of its own computations, a huge portion of today's forecasts for data centers, energy, and chip demand could quickly become irrelevant.

We're currently building hundreds of billions of dollars' worth of infrastructure based on how much computing power today's technologies require.

But what if tomorrow's technology suddenly requires 100 or 1,000 times less?

And what would happen to all the investments that the market today considers almost guaranteed winners of the AI revolution?

22 May marks the date the UK’s automatic organ donation system took effect: adults are considered donors unless they opt out. Many people may not know this.

That policy concerns donation after death. Emergency care is a separate matter. Claims that a patient’s medical history or perceived value to the system determines whether they receive life-saving treatment require evidence.

Understand how the rules work. Ask questions, and make an informed choice about opting in or out.
